guitar.evidence: Jimi Hendrix's white Fender Stratocaster (played upside-down/restrung for a right-handed guitar as a left-handed player) is one of the most iconic guitar associations in rock history.

tone.target: psychedelic fuzz wah lead with vibrato
tone.profile: psychedelic fuzz wah lead with vibrato
tone.summary: Fuzz -> Wah -> Boost/OD -> UK 45 Amp -> UK Vintage 4x12 Cab. Emphasis on raw, aggressive tones with vibrato modulation.

rig.name: Jimi Hendrix - Manic Depression - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up stray noise from high-gain fuzz and wah sweeps.
Provide the core psychedelic fuzz and raw 60s breakup required for the tone.
Implement the signature wah sweep and upper-mid bite.
Add controlled grit and boost the signal for lead lines without losing fuzz character.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is a general overdrive, but it helps maintain the 'raw' feel better than a standard Boost.

alternatives.reason: A slightly cleaner option if the fuzz becomes too overwhelming.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the Marshall/Plexi style amp required for classic 60s rock bite.
Provide the classic small-to-medium cab sound associated with the era.
Add the required Hendrix-style vibrato effect to lead lines.
Enhance the upper-mid bite and cut excessive low end, focusing on clarity.
Add subtle ambience without sounding modern or digital.
blocks.gap: The source material suggests a raw, dry sound, so the reverb is kept minimal to avoid muddying the fuzz.

alternatives.reason: A slightly brighter alternative if the room tone feels too dark.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism for a more authentic 60s British rock sound.

proposals.reason: Enhance the classic small-cab bite and vintage character missing from generic simulations.
